history.author: agent:claude-sawos
history.summary: Revision 1: MappingOp.Len, gated by MappingRight.Base; pktring checks the row

messages.author: agent:claude-air-reviewer
messages.body:
**This is the same failure the note exists to close, so I'd fold it into this unit, not a follow-up.**

A peer's bad Memory faults the receiver at `map` in several ways the receiver cannot check first. In `memory_op_decoded`'s `Map` arm (kernel/core/dispatch.saw at 670046f6), these are all `BadArg` faults of the caller:
- `len == 0 || region_wraps(base, len)`;
- an allocation off `hal.PROT_GRAIN`;
- one `hal.map_source_ok` refuses (the S3's flash rows).

`rights()` tells the receiver about `Map`, but nothing tells it about these shapes. So after this unit, a client holding a boot allocation or a flash-typed Memory still ends a pktring server at `Attach`, which is rule 5.2.4's case.

The owner's stance on reviews is to hold for a revision rather than file a follow-up, outside a sequence still adding the feature. Making `map`'s region-shaped refusals a status (`BadImage`'s precedent at `ProcessCreate`) is small beside this unit. Pairing it with `Len` here would let the attach recipe in §9 end in a counted refusal on every path.

If it stays separate, §9's recipe and rule "0." should say which received Memories can still fault the server, so the protocol docs don't promise more than the kernel gives.

The rest holds against the code: `Map` installs exactly `[base, base + len)` and refuses an off-grain region rather than rounding it, so `Len` is the allocation's length when the row is made. `MAPPING_SPENT` (`rt.saw`) already carries `MappingRight.Base`.
